liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (3 reviews): Reviewer ranks this Morning Dew among the best they have ever heard; Reviewer rates this Morning Dew among the best they have heard [13][16][17]
- **Good Lovin'** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls the Lesh and Garcia duet here possibly the most incredible one in recorded Dead history; Pigpen sings in very strong form here, despite the microphone trouble at the start [8][9][12]
- **St. Stephen** (3 reviews): Reviewer singles out the extended noodling jam in St. Stephen as unlike any other; After the 'One man gathers' verse, the band goes straight into Not Fade Away, as setlists indicate [7][8][9]
- **Dancin' In The Streets** (2 reviews): Reviewer praises the jams in this version, with raw Garcia playing; Reviewer finds this version unusually mind-expanding, with spontaneity and dynamics that few other versions match [7][11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Lost Kid Announcement/Tuning/Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-05-06.sbd.gans-hall.95.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 13 songs; 88 min; rated 4.13/5 by 15 [1]
- **gd70-05-06.sbd.gans.94.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 9 songs; 88 min; rated 4.51/5 by 49 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer hears the sound as slightly shaky, though the remastered digital copy sounds much better than an old cassette; Reviewer calls the recording excellent sounding, unlike quite a few other 1970 shows; Reviewer says the recording sounds good, with pleasing tape saturation [3][7][12][15]
- **gd1970-05-06.sbd.gmb.95816.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 88 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: The tape has a cut at the start of Dancin', and a reel-change cut in China Cat/Rider at 4:19; The first minute of Casey Jones is 2.5 dB quieter than the rest of the track [4]
- **gd1970-05-06.156178.msr.zootype.flac16**: source not stated; 12 songs; 88 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]

## Around the show

- At the start of Good Lovin', Pigpen tells the crowd that one nearby microphone works badly [8]
- The band played in cold weather [11]
- Pigpen sounded angry while commenting on a microphone glitch at the start of Good Lovin' [12]
- Free concert held amid nationwide campus strikes protesting the Kent State killings [2]
- Reviewer finds it decent but not among 1970's best; Dancin' and Good Lovin' are good, not standouts for the era [6]
- Reviewer ranks this Dancin' alongside the Cream Puff War performances and other legendary ones [11]
- Reviewer considers it no average 1970 show, among the most psychedelic they know, and the benchmark for other 1970 tapes [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-05-06.sbd.gans-hall.95.shnf**: transferred by David Gans and Mike Hall; source: MSR (MIT Reels) 1/2 Track Mono -> Otari MX 55 2 track (playback) -> TC 2000 Studio Effects Processor (using only the A->D converter, no effects) ->Sonic… [1]
- **gd70-05-06.sbd.gans.94.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Eli Polonsky, Rango Keshavan and Darrin Sacks; source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Source is the MIT WMBR 10-inch mono reels, played on an Otari MX 55 and digitized through a TC 2000 converter; Transfer passed via E. Polonsky, D. Gans, R. Keshavan and D. Sacks, then CD from Gans, to EAC and SHN [3]
- **gd1970-05-06.sbd.gmb.95816.flac16**: transferred by Bill Koucky; source: Master Soundboard Reels 10", 2-sided, 1/2 Track Mono > DAT x 1 [4]. Also: Eli Polansky transferred the WMBR MIT Radio Archives reels to DAT in 1994 for Jim Birkhead, cloned to Bill Koucky [4]
- **gd1970-05-06.156178.msr.zootype.flac16**: transferred by Zootype; source: MSR (MIT Reels) > Sonic Solutions Digital Editing (gans) > DATs > CDRs > EAC > SHN [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by rahvaraamat.ee: [Grateful Dead - Kresge Plaza, M.I.T. Cambridge, M.A., May 6, 1970 WMBR (2024) CD - Rahva Raamat](https://rahvaraamat.ee/et/muusika/muusika/poprock/grateful-dead-kresge-plaza-mit-cambridge-ma-may-6-1970-wmbr-2024/2493090) [19]
